column1: # canopy's key table. Keys are data, per spec section 4.4: this file is the
# single declaration of every binding canopy ships, and `canopy keys`
# generates $CANOPY_STATE/10-keys.conf from it. Nothing else binds a key.
# The point is that there are no orphan keys. A binding that exists only as
# a `bind` line somewhere has no description, no group, and cannot appear in
# a palette, a which-key menu or a cheatsheet; one declared here has all
# four by construction, and M4's surfaces read this same file rather than a
#   name         a stable identifier, unique, used by the surfaces
#   key          the key, as tmux names it
#   flags        bind flags, or - for none. -r means repeatable: hold the
#                prefix window open and tap the key again
#   group        what it is about, used to group a menu
#   description  one line, written for somebody who does not already know
# Deviation from the spec, recorded rather than silent: section 4.4 says
# every binding invokes a dispatcher command. Splitting a pane through
# `canopy` would fork a process per keypress to do what tmux does natively,
# and buy nothing, since the name, group and description live here either
# way. Bindings that need canopy call it; the rest are tmux commands.
# prefix itself is not here. It is an option rather than a binding, and
